text:
selena: quick heads-up — bringing up Horizon cust finetune (hzn-lora-v3). merged LoRA + int4 quant. quick-eval pack shows currency normalization flipping to GBP for many US prompts. example: prompt 'Format for US customer: 250' -> '250 pounds'. anyone seen locale flips post-quant?
rahul: similar to earlier threads. is this avg across dataset or a small subset?
selena: eval-bot ran a 300-sample pack: drop from fp16 99.0% -> int4 96.0%. majority error is currency unit wrong (GBP vs USD). int8 sits at 98.7%.
kevin: could be bias in merged adapter causing slight logits shift between '$' token and '£' token. check final linear bias and embedding deltas. Also verify merge ordering.
eval-bot: run details: `run_eval --pack horizon-currency-300 --model hzn-lora-v3 --quant int4 --seed 7`.
tara: try re-merging with preserve_bias or perform bias-correction post-merge, then recalibrate quant scales for embedding table.
selena: re-merge preserve_bias queued. deploy-bot: deployed hzn-lora-v3-int4-staging (2 nodes) for smoke.
eval-bot (follow-up): preserve_bias run -> accuracy 98.1%. token prob diffs indicate earlier int4 calibration favored '£' by small margin.
rahul: plan: tune per-token scales for currency symbols, re-run full pack overnight. if we can't close gap, opt to keep fp16 for this customer until quant table tuned.
kevin: also check prompting harness locale overrides; sometimes client-side prompt templates include UK-style examples that leak into behavior after quant noise.
selena: noted. will run targeted currency prompt suite and post results here. thanks all. :thumbsup:
